solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Help to drink wine

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone is offered assistance in the form of a glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To support someone is to back or assist them, a straightforward synonym of help.

clue.text: He looks as though he hasn't washed the back of the neck

definitions.text: He looks as though he hasn't washed

definitions.meaning: the nape, as in grabbed by the ... of the neck

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a grubby, unkempt person and the nape by which one is grabbed.

clue.text: No single word will fit here

definitions.text: No single word will fit here

parts.words: No single word will fit here
parts.note: the grammatical number for more than one excludes any word in the singular

explanation.surface: A setter complains that no one word fits the space in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural noun form is by definition never singular, the grammatical number for more than one.

clue.text: Too far into no-man's-land?

definitions.meaning: in the First World War troops climbed out of the trench parapet into no-man's-land

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means excessive and, literally, the charge out of the trenches in wartime.

clue.text: Roots developing into a trunk

indicators.note: developing means the letters grow into a new form

explanation.surface: A tree's roots grow up into its main stem.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a tree, but the trunk is the human body without head or limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the human body's main section, also called the trunk.

clue.text: Won't he be found out?

parts.note: read literally, someone who is never found outside, i.e. one who is always within the group

explanation.surface: A worry about whether a wrongdoer will be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cheat afraid of exposure; the cryptic reading is a person who is never to be found 'out', because he is on the inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person inside an organisation, privy to its secrets, is never outside it.

clue.text: Cecil and I chewed cold tongue

indicators.note: chewed means the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people ate a chilled serving of ox tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold tongue' reads like meat on a plate, but it is the language of a cold country.
explanation.definitionFit: Icelandic is the language spoken in Iceland, a famously cold country.

clue.text: A swimmer — the only one to be seen

definitions.meaning: a flatfish, so a creature that swims

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a flatfish and also means one and only.

clue.text: Issue dad is out to advise against

indicators.note: out here means the letters are put out of their places

explanation.surface: A child is set to talk a father out of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissuade someone is to persuade them not to do something.

clue.text: Magazine in colour given back

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: red is a colour
a magazine is a storehouse for arms, a store

explanation.surface: A glossy publication printed in colour is returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something restored has been returned to its owner or former condition.

clue.text: The way to get out and about outside

indicators.note: outside tells us the word for about goes around the other piece

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Directions for escaping and wandering around in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a path or course taken to reach somewhere, a synonym of way.

clue.text: Joins forces again to disturb listeners

indicators.note: to disturb the letters is to throw them out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone signs up once more just to annoy the radio audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enlist is to sign up for the armed forces a second time.

clue.text: Part of trial can collapse

indicators.note: a collapse leaves the letters fallen into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Part of a court case may fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' looks like a selection signal, but 'of' is fodder and 'Part' alone is the definition, in its adjectival sense as in a part payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fractional is only a portion of a whole, as in partial or part.

clue.text: One short month to love a beautiful woman

indicators.note: short means the month's name loses its final letter

parts.note: June is the sixth month
love is nil, and so the letter O, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A brief time in summer spent courting a lovely lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A Juno is a stately, beautiful woman, after the queen of the Roman gods.

clue.text: Some analytical piecework?

parts.note: work that cuts something into pieces in order to analyse it

explanation.surface: A description of piecework done with an analyst's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissection means cutting a body into parts for study, and also close analysis.

clue.text: Minor role in yet another swindle

parts.note: a second one is yet another of the same
a fiddle is a dishonest scheme, a swindle

explanation.surface: A small part is cast in one more scam.
explanation.definitionFit: To play second fiddle is to take a subordinate, supporting part.

clue.text: Frank gets contract showing unlimited resources

parts.note: frank means open, candid
to purse one's lips is to contract them

explanation.surface: An honest person is given a deal that shows they have unlimited money.
explanation.definitionFit: An open purse suggests money available without limit.

clue.text: It meant sentence of death or some bird

definitions.meaning: the ... was worn by English judges passing a death sentence
a warbler with a black crown

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a judge's death-sentence headgear and to a small songbird.

clue.text: Gold in finals round? Quite the opposite, producing serious complaint

indicators.note: in signals putting one piece inside another
says the insertion runs the other way, so the scrambled finals go inside gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: round means the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A sportsman asks about gold in the last round and suffers a nasty illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold in finals round' would put gold inside the scrambled word; 'Quite the opposite' flips that, so the scrambled finals sit inside gold's symbol. The 1957 pandemic began in East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Asian flu was a serious influenza pandemic of the late 1950s, so a grave illness.

clue.text: Find luggage missing but fail to get legal redress

definitions.meaning: a case is a suitcase, and one may lose it
a lawsuit is a case, and a litigant may lose it in court

explanation.surface: A traveller's bags go astray and the lawsuit over it fails too.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works for both a mislaid suitcase and a court action that ends in defeat.

clue.text: Capital city — the Big Smoke?

definitions.meaning: a large cigar; the Big Smoke is also a nickname for London

explanation.walkthrough: The Big Smoke is a British nickname for London, which pushes towards a capital city; here it is a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: It is Cuba's capital and the name for a fine Cuban cigar, a big smoke.

clue.text: Negotiate a rise?

parts.note: to negotiate a hill is to get up it, not to bargain for more pay

explanation.surface: An employee wonders about bargaining for a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to climb, to get up or over a slope.

clue.text: Stuff to study for an exam

definitions.meaning: to stuff is to pack something tightly full
to swot hard at the last minute before a test

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both packing tightly and intensive last-minute revision.

clue.text: Aristocratic sixth form?

definitions.meaning: belonging to the nobility or gentry
in British schools the sixth form is the top, or senior, form of students

explanation.walkthrough: The British sixth form is the final two years of secondary school, so it is the upper level of classes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the social elite and, punningly, the top classes of a school.

clue.text: Outdated law, to be precise

parts.note: ex means former, no longer current
an act is a law passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: An obsolete statute is cited, to be accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means accurate in every detail, a synonym of precise.

clue.text: Some private tuition that's for benefit of the seamstress

definitions.text: that's for benefit of the seamstress

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dressmaker profits from some private lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and sewing items, useful to a needlewoman.

clue.text: The only waiting here is at the counter

definitions.text: The only waiting here is at the counter

parts.words: The only waiting here is at the counter
parts.note: in a self-service eatery nobody serves at table; diners queue at the counter instead

explanation.surface: A remark about a restaurant where nobody serves at the tables.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service restaurant where customers collect food from a counter.

clue.text: One thousand years old statue?

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
the Roman numeral M is a thousand
one's age is how many years old one is

explanation.surface: A question about whether a sculpture is a thousand and one years old.
explanation.definitionFit: An image can be a carved likeness or effigy, such as an idol or statue.

clue.text: She may be used to describe Biblical epistles

definitions.meaning: a girl's name, so a possible she
the letters of St Paul in the New Testament are given an adjective from his name

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a woman's first name and the adjective for writings of the apostle Paul.

clue.text: Volunteers drank rum — from this?

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: rum here is the adjective meaning odd or strange, so the letters are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: The reserve soldiers knocked back spirits and we ask what vessel they used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the anagram signal, turning DRANK into NKARD; the whole clue also describes the pewter mug.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a large beer mug, which soldiers might drink from.
